A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Hubbard model is an effective model of a Fermi liquid, and not an effective model of the pairing interaction.

the three-band Hubbard Hamiltonian is the minimal model to describe the Cu-O plane and that the pairing of two holes is an intrinsic instability of the system, which can be described analytically in the framework of a renormalized perturbation theory.

the three-band Hubbard Hamiltonian is the most suitable starting point for the description of the Cu-O-plane, and that a canonical transformation is the most natural way to obtain an effective model of two holes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Hubbard model is not a good starting point for the theory of the Cu-O planes, and that a three-band Hamiltonian is needed to describe correctly the low-energy physics of these systems.

, in contrast to the two-band Hubbard model, the three-band model is capable of describing the pairing of holes in the Cu-O plane, which is the essential ingredient in the mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity in the cuprates.
, contrary to what is often believed, the Hubbard model of the Cu-O planes is capable of describing the formation of a bound state of two holes.
